docs.title: ThingLarp Documentation
docs.text:
Welcome to ThingLarp, a fast, unconstrained IoT telemetry platform built as an open modern alternative to ThingSpeak.

ThingLarp lets you connect microcontrollers, sensors, and hardware devices to ingest data over standard HTTP REST or MQTT, store time-series metrics with zero rate limits, and visualize your feeds on a real-time web dashboard.

docs.title: Why ThingLarp?
docs.text: Feature Legacy IoT Platforms ThingLarp Update Rate Limit 1 update every 15–60 seconds Zero artificial rate limits (stream up to 100Hz) Field Constraints Rigid 8 fields (field1...field8) Unlimited dynamic JSON fields (auto-discovered) Visualizations Static charts Real-time live streaming (QoS 1 WebSockets / MQTT) Public Sharing Complex or locked 1-click public share links for any browser Downlink Control Paid addon Built-in hardware commands

docs.title: 3-Minute Quickstart
docs.text: Getting sensor readings streaming into ThingLarp takes 3 simple steps:

docs.title: 1. Create a Channel
docs.text: Open the ThingLarp Web Dashboard, sign in, and click + New Channel. Give it a name like "Weather Station".

docs.title: 2. Get an API Key or Device Credentials
docs.text:
• For HTTP REST: Open your channel, go to the API Keys tab, and copy your channel's API key.
  • For MQTT: Go to the Devices tab, click Provision Device, and save the generated MQTT username (d_xxxx) and password.

docs.title: 3. Send Telemetry
docs.text:
Send a JSON payload with your sensor readings:

cURL (HTTP)Python (HTTP)MQTT (CLI) 
curl -X POST https://api.iimarky123.io.vn/channels/YOUR_CHANNEL_ID/data \
  -H "X-API-Key: YOUR_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"temperature": 25.4, "humidity": 62.1, "pressure_hpa": 1013.2}'

import requests

requests.post(
    "https://api.iimarky123.io.vn/channels/YOUR_CHANNEL_ID/data",
    headers={"X-API-Key": "YOUR_API_KEY"},
    json={"temperature": 25.4, "humidity": 62.1, "pressure_hpa": 1013.2}
)

mosquitto_pub -h mqtt.iimarky123.io.vn -p 8883 \
  -u "YOUR_DEVICE_USER" -P "YOUR_DEVICE_PASS" \
  -t "channels/YOUR_CHANNEL_ID/data" \
  -m '{"temperature": 25.4, "humidity": 62.1}'

docs.title: Explore the Guides
docs.text:
• Quickstart & First Steps: Account setup, channel management, and field options.
  • Web Dashboard: Real-time charts, widget customization, and CSV export.
  • Public Link Sharing: Sharing live telemetry with anyone on the web.
  • HTTP Ingestion: Complete guide to sending data using HTTP REST API.
  • MQTT Ingestion: High-speed telemetry streaming with MQTT.
  • Hardware Examples: Arduino C++ (ESP32/ESP8266), MicroPython, and Python code.
  • REST API Reference: Detailed endpoints, queries, and responses.

docs.title: Web Dashboard & Charts
docs.text: The ThingLarp Web Dashboard at https://thinglarp.iimarky123.io.vn/app/ provides real-time visualizations and channel management directly in your browser.

docs.title: Live Telemetry Streaming
docs.text: When you open a channel: - The dashboard automatically opens a secure WebSocket stream (wss://mqtt.iimarky123.io.vn/mqtt) with QoS 1. - The top status bar indicates: - Streaming Live Data (QoS 1): Real-time sensor updates push directly to the chart. - Pause / Resume: You can pause the live stream to inspect a specific historical snapshot.

docs.title: Field Widgets & Visualizations
docs.text: Every auto-discovered field gets a metric card displaying its latest value, unit, and time-series line chart.

docs.title: Customizing Widget Types
docs.text:
Owners can customize how each metric is rendered by clicking the Tune icon (⋮) on any field card:

Widget Type Best For Visual Representation Line Chart (default) Continuous time-series Interactive line chart with min/max/average markers Gauge Percentage or bounded ranges (0–100%) Radial dial with warning thresholds Bar Chart Discrete readings, counts, energy consumption Categorical vertical bars Status Card / KPI On/off states, alarms, counters Large bold display with live trend indicator

docs.title: Adjusting Query Resolution
docs.text: The dashboard features an automatic rollup selector: - Auto Resolution: Automatically chooses the ideal rollup (raw, 1-minute, or 1-hour) based on data volume. - Raw Points: Displays exact microsecond data points. - 1-min Averages: Continuous rollup averages calculated every 60 seconds. - 1-hour Averages: Ideal for viewing multi-week or multi-month historical trends.

docs.title: Exporting & Importing Data
docs.text: From the channel menu (⋮ in the top right of the channel screen):

docs.title: 1. Download / Export Data
docs.text:
• Export all historical telemetry as standard CSV format.
  • Select date range and limit (up to 10,000 points per export).
  • Ideal for analysis in Python (pandas), Excel, MATLAB, or Jupyter notebooks.

docs.title: 2. Import CSV Data
docs.text:
• Bulk-upload historical CSV data into your channel.
  • Automatically handles ISO-8601 timestamps and key-value mapping.

docs.title: 3. Clear Telemetry Data
docs.text: • Clears all collected historical points for the channel while preserving provisioned devices and field customizations.

docs.title: Getting Started with ThingLarp
docs.text: This guide walks you through setting up your account, creating your first channel, and understanding how data is structured in ThingLarp.

docs.title: 1. Access the Dashboard
docs.text:
Navigate to https://thinglarp.iimarky123.io.vn/app/ in any modern web browser.

  • If you already have an account, enter your username and password.
  • If you are new, click Register to create a free account.

docs.title: 2. Channels Explained
docs.text:
In ThingLarp, a Channel is the container for all telemetry sent by your devices or sensors (similar to a project or data stream).

Each channel has: - Channel ID: A unique numeric ID (e.g., 42) used in API endpoints and MQTT topics. - Name & Description: Human-readable label for your dashboard. - Visibility: - Private (default): Only you can read or publish telemetry. - Public: Anyone with the link can view live charts and historical feeds without logging in.

docs.title: Creating a Channel
docs.text:
1. In the channels overview screen, click + New Channel.
  2. Enter a name (e.g., Greenhouse Sensor).
  3. Optionally add a description.
  4. Toggle Public Channel if you want to share real-time telemetry with colleagues or the public.
  5. Click Create.

docs.title: 3. Dynamic Field Auto-Discovery
docs.text:
Unlike traditional IoT platforms where you must manually pre-configure field1, field2, etc., ThingLarp features dynamic schema discovery.

When your sensor publishes a JSON payload: 

{
  "temp_c": 24.8,
  "humidity_pct": 58.2,
  "soil_moisture": 420
}

ThingLarp automatically: 1. Detects each new key (temp_c, humidity_pct, soil_moisture). 2. Registers them as channel fields in the database. 3. Automatically generates responsive UI widgets and real-time line charts on your dashboard. 4. Indexes data into continuous 1-minute and 1-hour aggregate views for instantaneous chart rendering.

docs.title: 4. Choosing How to Connect Your Device
docs.text:
ThingLarp supports two ingestion methods:

  1. HTTP REST API:

    • Ideal for microcontrollers or webhooks that send periodic updates over HTTPS (e.g., every 10 seconds or 1 minute).
    • Requires an API Key generated from the channel's API Keys tab.
    • Read the HTTP Ingestion Guide.

  2. MQTT Broker:

    • Ideal for high-speed streaming (1Hz – 100Hz) or battery-conscious edge hardware.
    • Requires Device Credentials provisioned from the channel's Devices tab.
    • Read the MQTT Ingestion Guide.

docs.title: Public Channel Link Sharing
docs.text: ThingLarp allows you to share live telemetry dashboards with clients, colleagues, or the public without requiring them to register an account.

docs.title: 1-Click Share Links
docs.text:
You can share any channel using direct deep-link URLs:

https://thinglarp.iimarky123.io.vn/app/#/channel/{channel_id}

docs.title: How to Copy the Share Link
docs.text:
1. Open your channel in the Web Dashboard or native app.
  2. Tap the Share icon (🔗 / Icons.share) in the top app bar or next to your channel card.
  3. The public link is automatically copied to your clipboard.

Private Channel Warning

If your channel is currently marked as Private, clicking the share button will display a prompt asking if you want to Make Channel Public. Anyone who opens a private link will see an Access Denied screen unless you toggle the channel to Public.

docs.title: Read-Only Public Viewer Mode
docs.text:
When an unauthenticated visitor opens a public link in any desktop or mobile browser:

  • Full Live Telemetry: All sensor fields, latest values, and time-series charts load instantly.
  • Auto-Refresh: Telemetry polls automatically every 10 seconds to keep charts up to date.
  • Privacy Protection:
  • The Devices tab is hidden (device MQTT credentials are never exposed).
  • The API Keys tab is hidden (write keys are protected).
  • Channel deletion and field editing buttons are disabled.
  • Quick Sign-In: An explicit Sign In button is visible in the header so registered owners can jump into edit mode at any time.

docs.title: HTTP REST Ingestion
docs.text: Sending telemetry to ThingLarp via HTTP is simple and requires only a single POST request.

docs.title: Ingestion Endpoint
docs.text: POST https://api.iimarky123.io.vn/channels/{channel_id}/data

docs.title: Authentication Header
docs.text:
Provide your Channel API Key in the X-API-Key header: 

X-API-Key: tl_ak_xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx
Content-Type: application/json

docs.title: Payload Format
docs.text:
Send arbitrary JSON key-value pairs. Numeric values (integers, floats) are charted automatically.

{
  "temperature": 24.85,
  "humidity": 61.2,
  "co2_ppm": 412,
  "battery_v": 3.78
}

docs.title: Response
docs.text:
On success, the API returns 202 Accepted: 

{
  "status": "accepted",
  "channel_id": 42
}

docs.title: 1. cURL (CLI)
docs.text:
curl -X POST "https://api.iimarky123.io.vn/channels/42/data" \
  -H "X-API-Key: tl_ak_YOUR_API_KEY_HERE" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"temperature": 24.8, "humidity": 60.5}'

docs.title: 2. Python (requests)
docs.text:
import requests

API_URL = "https://api.iimarky123.io.vn/channels/42/data"
API_KEY = "tl_ak_YOUR_API_KEY_HERE"

payload = {
    "temperature": 24.8,
    "humidity": 60.5,
    "soil_moisture": 380
}

response = requests.post(
    API_URL,
    headers={"X-API-Key": API_KEY},
    json=payload
)

print(f"Status: {response.status_code}")

docs.title: 3. JavaScript / Node.js (fetch)
docs.text:
const res = await fetch("https://api.iimarky123.io.vn/channels/42/data", {
  method: "POST",
  headers: {
    "X-API-Key": "tl_ak_YOUR_API_KEY_HERE",
    "Content-Type": "application/json"
  },
  body: JSON.stringify({
    temperature: 24.8,
    humidity: 60.5
  })
});

console.log(`Status: ${res.status}`);

docs.title: Querying Historical Telemetry
docs.text: You can read back recent points directly via HTTP:

docs.title: Latest Values Snapshot
docs.text:
curl -X GET "https://api.iimarky123.io.vn/channels/42/latest" \
  -H "X-API-Key: tl_ak_YOUR_API_KEY_HERE"

docs.title: Feeds History Query
docs.text:
curl -X GET "https://api.iimarky123.io.vn/channels/42/history?limit=50&order=desc" \
  -H "X-API-Key: tl_ak_YOUR_API_KEY_HERE"
(If your channel is marked as Public, the X-API-Key header can be omitted on read queries!)

docs.title: MQTT Ingestion
docs.text: For high-frequency sensor streams (1Hz–100Hz) or battery-powered microcontrollers, MQTT provides low network overhead, instant delivery, and bidirectional communication.

docs.title: Connection Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Production Value Description Broker Host mqtt.iimarky123.io.vn Domain for the MQTT broker TCP Port (TLS) 8883 Secure TLS connection for ESP32 & native apps WebSocket Port 443 Secure WSS (/mqtt) for web browsers Username d_xxxxxxxxx Device-specific username provisioned in your channel Password (random 32-char token) Generated during device provisioning Telemetry Topic channels/{channel_id}/data Topic to publish sensor JSON readings QoS Level 0 or 1 QoS 1 recommended for guaranteed delivery

docs.title: Provisioning a Device
docs.text:
1. Open your channel in the Web Dashboard.
  2. Select the Devices tab.
  3. Click Provision New Device.
  4. Choose an access scope:
  5. Publish (Pub): Device can only publish sensor readings.
  6. Pub/Sub: Device can publish telemetry and receive downlink commands.
  7. Click Generate Credentials and copy the username and password.

docs.title: Publishing Telemetry
docs.text:
Publish a standard JSON object to: 

channels/{channel_id}/data

docs.title: CLI Example with mosquitto_pub
docs.text:
mosquitto_pub \
  -h mqtt.iimarky123.io.vn \
  -p 8883 \
  -u "d_YOUR_DEVICE_USER" \
  -P "YOUR_DEVICE_PASS" \
  -t "channels/42/data" \
  -m '{"rpm": 1250, "vibration_g": 0.042, "current_a": 3.12}' \
  -q 1

Once published, the data is ingested into TimescaleDB within milliseconds and pushed to all active web and mobile viewers listening on that channel.

docs.title: Downlink Commands (Device Control)
docs.text: ThingLarp allows you to send downlink control messages from the Web Dashboard or API directly to edge devices (e.g. toggling relays, updating sensor sample intervals, or triggering reboots).

docs.title: 1. Device Setup for Downlinks
docs.text: When provisioning your device in the dashboard: - Ensure the access scope is set to Subscribe (Sub) or Pub/Sub. - Devices with Publish-only scope cannot subscribe to downlink topics.

docs.title: Device Topic to Subscribe:
docs.text: channels/{channel_id}/commands

docs.title: 2. Sending a Command from the Dashboard
docs.text:
1. Open your channel in the Web Dashboard.
  2. In the top action bar, click the Downlink Commands icon (📲).
  3. Select the target device (or all), enter the command name (e.g., relay_1) and parameters ({"state": "ON"}).
  4. Click Dispatch Command.

docs.title: 3. Sending a Command via HTTP API
docs.text:
You can trigger a downlink programmatically via HTTP:

curl -X POST "https://api.iimarky123.io.vn/channels/42/commands" \
  -H "X-API-Key: tl_ak_YOUR_API_KEY_HERE" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "command": "set_interval",
    "params": {"interval_sec": 10},
    "target_device": "esp32_node_1"
  }'

docs.title: 4. Handling Commands on ESP32 (Arduino C++)
docs.text:
void onMessage(char* topic, byte* payload, unsigned int length) {
  String message;
  for (int i = 0; i < length; i++) {
    message += (char)payload[i];
  }
  Serial.println("Command received: " + message);

  StaticJsonDocument<200> doc;
  deserializeJson(doc, message);

  const char* cmd = doc["command"];
  if (strcmp(cmd, "relay_1") == 0) {
    bool state = doc["params"]["state"] == "ON";
    digitalWrite(LED_BUILTIN, state ? HIGH : LOW);
  }
}

void setup() {
  // ... wifi setup ...
  client.setCallback(onMessage);
  client.subscribe("channels/42/commands");
}

docs.title: ESP32 / Arduino C++ Integration
docs.text: This guide provides complete, production-ready Arduino C++ code to stream sensor data from an ESP32 or ESP8266 to ThingLarp using WiFi and MQTT.

docs.title: Required Libraries
docs.text: Install via the Arduino Library Manager: - PubSubClient by Nick O'Leary - ArduinoJson (v6 or v7) by Benoît Blanchon

docs.title: Complete Arduino C++ Code
docs.text:
#include <WiFi.h>
#include <WiFiClientSecure.h>
#include <PubSubClient.h>
#include <ArduinoJson.h>

// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Configuration
// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
const char* WIFI_SSID     = "YOUR_WIFI_SSID";
const char* WIFI_PASS     = "YOUR_WIFI_PASSWORD";

const char* MQTT_BROKER   = "mqtt.iimarky123.io.vn";
const int   MQTT_PORT     = 8883;

// Device credentials from ThingLarp Dashboard -> Devices tab
const char* MQTT_USER     = "d_YOUR_DEVICE_USER";
const char* MQTT_PASS     = "YOUR_DEVICE_PASSWORD";

const int   CHANNEL_ID    = 42; // Replace with your Channel ID
const char* DATA_TOPIC    = "channels/42/data";

// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Networking
// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
WiFiClientSecure net;
PubSubClient client(net);
unsigned long lastPublish = 0;

void setupWifi() {
  Serial.print("Connecting to WiFi: ");
  Serial.println(WIFI_SSID);
  WiFi.begin(WIFI_SSID, WIFI_PASS);

  while (WiFi.status() != WL_CONNECTED) {
    delay(500);
    Serial.print(".");
  }
  Serial.println("\nWiFi connected! IP: " + WiFi.localIP().toString());

  // Insecure mode for simple deployments without bundle cert
  net.setInsecure();
}

void reconnectMqtt() {
  while (!client.connected()) {
    Serial.print("Connecting to ThingLarp MQTT...");
    String clientId = "ESP32_" + String(random(0xffff), HEX);

    if (client.connect(clientId.c_str(), MQTT_USER, MQTT_PASS)) {
      Serial.println(" Connected!");
    } else {
      Serial.print(" Failed, rc=");
      Serial.print(client.state());
      Serial.println(" Retrying in 5 seconds...");
      delay(5000);
    }
  }
}

void setup() {
  Serial.begin(115200);
  setupWifi();
  client.setServer(MQTT_BROKER, MQTT_PORT);
}

void loop() {
  if (!client.connected()) {
    reconnectMqtt();
  }
  client.loop();

  // Publish sensor reading every 5 seconds
  if (millis() - lastPublish > 5000) {
    lastPublish = millis();

    // Read your sensors here
    float temp = 25.0 + (random(-20, 20) / 10.0);
    float humidity = 60.0 + (random(-50, 50) / 10.0);
    int lightRaw = analogRead(34);

    // Build JSON payload
    StaticJsonDocument<200> doc;
    doc["temperature"] = temp;
    doc["humidity"] = humidity;
    doc["light_adc"] = lightRaw;

    char buffer[256];
    serializeJson(doc, buffer);

    Serial.print("Publishing: ");
    Serial.println(buffer);
    client.publish(DATA_TOPIC, buffer, false);
  }
}

docs.title: MicroPython Integration
docs.text: This guide provides a minimal script to stream sensor telemetry to ThingLarp using MicroPython on an ESP32 or Raspberry Pi Pico W.

docs.title: Required Library
docs.text:
Ensure umqtt.simple is installed: 

import mip
mip.install("umqtt.simple")

docs.title: Complete MicroPython Script
docs.text:
import time
import ujson
import network
import urandom
from umqtt.simple import MQTTClient

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Configuration
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
WIFI_SSID = "YOUR_WIFI_SSID"
WIFI_PASS = "YOUR_WIFI_PASSWORD"

BROKER_HOST = "mqtt.iimarky123.io.vn"
BROKER_PORT = 8883

CHANNEL_ID = 42
DEVICE_USER = "d_YOUR_DEVICE_USER"
DEVICE_PASS = "YOUR_DEVICE_PASSWORD"
TOPIC = f"channels/{CHANNEL_ID}/data"

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Connect WiFi
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
wlan = network.WLAN(network.STA_IF)
wlan.active(True)
wlan.connect(WIFI_SSID, WIFI_PASS)

print("Connecting to WiFi...", end="")
while not wlan.isconnected():
    time.sleep(0.5)
    print(".", end="")
print(f"\nWiFi connected: {wlan.ifconfig()[0]}")

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Connect MQTT & Publish Loop
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
client_id = f"pico_{urandom.getrandbits(16):04x}"
client = MQTTClient(
    client_id=client_id,
    server=BROKER_HOST,
    port=BROKER_PORT,
    user=DEVICE_USER,
    password=DEVICE_PASS,
    ssl=True,
    ssl_params={"server_hostname": BROKER_HOST}
)

client.connect()
print("Connected to ThingLarp Broker!")

while True:
    # Read hardware sensors
    temp = 24.5 + (urandom.getrandbits(8) % 30) / 10.0
    humidity = 58.0 + (urandom.getrandbits(8) % 40) / 10.0

    payload = {
        "temperature": temp,
        "humidity": humidity,
        "device_status": "online"
    }

    raw_json = ujson.dumps(payload)
    print("Publishing:", raw_json)
    client.publish(TOPIC, raw_json)

    time.sleep(5)

docs.title: Python Scripting Integration
docs.text: Stream telemetry from a Raspberry Pi, edge gateway, or Linux server to ThingLarp using Python.

docs.title: 1. Using MQTT (paho-mqtt)
docs.text:
pip install paho-mqtt

import time
import json
import random
import paho.mqtt.client as mqtt

BROKER_HOST = "mqtt.iimarky123.io.vn"
BROKER_PORT = 8883
CHANNEL_ID = 42

DEVICE_USER = "d_YOUR_DEVICE_USER"
DEVICE_PASS = "YOUR_DEVICE_PASSWORD"
TOPIC = f"channels/{CHANNEL_ID}/data"

def on_connect(client, userdata, flags, rc):
    if rc == 0:
        print("Connected to ThingLarp Broker!")
    else:
        print(f"Connection failed, rc={rc}")

client = mqtt.Client(client_id=f"python_worker_{random.randint(1000, 9999)}")
client.username_pw_set(DEVICE_USER, DEVICE_PASS)
client.tls_set() # Enable TLS
client.on_connect = on_connect

client.connect(BROKER_HOST, BROKER_PORT, keepalive=60)
client.loop_start()

try:
    while True:
        payload = {
            "cpu_temperature": 48.2 + random.uniform(-1.5, 1.5),
            "ram_usage_pct": 34.1 + random.uniform(-0.5, 0.5),
            "disk_free_gb": 112.4
        }

        print("Publishing:", payload)
        client.publish(TOPIC, json.dumps(payload), qos=1)
        time.sleep(5)
except KeyboardInterrupt:
    client.loop_stop()
    client.disconnect()

docs.title: 2. Using HTTP REST (requests)
docs.text:
pip install requests

import time
import requests

API_URL = "https://api.iimarky123.io.vn/channels/42/data"
API_KEY = "tl_ak_YOUR_API_KEY_HERE"

while True:
    payload = {
        "metric_a": 12.4,
        "metric_b": 98.1
    }

    res = requests.post(
        API_URL,
        headers={"X-API-Key": API_KEY},
        json=payload,
        timeout=10
    )

    print(f"Sent: {payload} | Status: {res.status_code}")
    time.sleep(10)

docs.title: REST API Specification
docs.text: The REST API is exposed by the FastAPI Gateway service at http://localhost:8000 (or https://api.yourdomain.com).

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
All protected endpoints require an HTTP Authorization header containing a valid Bearer token:

Authorization: Bearer <ACCESS_TOKEN>

docs.title: Public Auth Configuration
docs.text:
GET /auth/config
Returns public authentication settings, such as whether self-registration is enabled. Does not require authentication.

Response (200 OK): 

{
  "registration_enabled": true
}

docs.title: Register User
docs.text:
POST /auth/register
Note: If public registration is locked by an administrator, this endpoint rejects requests with 403 Forbidden (detail: "Public registration is currently disabled by system administrator").

Request Body: 

{
  "username": "alice",
  "password": "Password123!"
}
Response (201 Created): 
{
  "id": 1,
  "username": "alice",
  "created_at": "2026-11-12T00:00:00Z"
}

docs.title: Login (Obtain Tokens)
docs.text:
POST /auth/login
Request Body: 
{
  "username": "alice",
  "password": "Password123!"
}
Response (200 OK): 
{
  "access_token": "eyJhbGciOi...",
  "refresh_token": "Au1R5Xk...",
  "token_type": "bearer",
  "expires_in_minutes": 15
}

docs.title: Refresh Access Token
docs.text:
POST /auth/refresh
Request Body: 
{
  "refresh_token": "Au1R5Xk..."
}
Response (200 OK): Returns fresh access_token.

docs.title: List User Channels
docs.text:
GET /channels
Response (200 OK): Array of Channel objects.

docs.title: Create Channel
docs.text:
POST /channels
Request Body: 
{
  "name": "Greenhouse Alpha",
  "description": "Climate and moisture monitoring",
  "is_public": false
}

docs.title: Get Channel Details
docs.text: GET /channels/{channel_id}

docs.title: List Channel Fields
docs.text:
GET /channels/{channel_id}/fields
Response (200 OK): 
[
  {
    "id": 1,
    "channel_id": 1,
    "key": "temperature",
    "label": "Ambient Temp",
    "unit": "°C",
    "value_type": "number",
    "widget_type": "line",
    "first_seen_at": "2026-11-12T04:38:34Z"
  }
]

docs.title: Update Channel Field Metadata & Widget Type
docs.text:
PATCH /channels/{channel_id}/fields/{field_id}
Authorization: Bearer <jwt_access_token>
Request Body: 
{
  "label": "Living Room Temp",
  "unit": "°C",
  "widget_type": "gauge"
}
widget_type accepts line, gauge, kpi, or status.

docs.title: List Devices
docs.text: GET /channels/{channel_id}/devices

docs.title: Provision Device
docs.text:
POST /channels/{channel_id}/devices
Request Body: 
{
  "name": "ESP32_Outdoor_Unit",
  "scope": "pubsub"
}
scope accepts publish (default), subscribe, or pubsub.

Response (201 Created): 

{
  "id": 1,
  "channel_id": 1,
  "name": "ESP32_Outdoor_Unit",
  "scope": "pubsub",
  "is_active": true,
  "mqtt_username": "dev_ch1_1",
  "mqtt_password": "<generated_password>",
  "created_at": "2026-11-12T04:38:34Z"
}

docs.title: Update Device Access Control & Status
docs.text:
PATCH /channels/{channel_id}/devices/{device_id}
Authorization: Bearer <jwt_access_token>
Request Body: 
{
  "name": "ESP32_Outdoor_Unit_Renamed",
  "scope": "pubsub",
  "is_active": true
}
scope accepts publish, subscribe, or pubsub. Setting is_active: false immediately denies MQTT authentication.

Response (200 OK): 

{
  "id": 1,
  "channel_id": 1,
  "name": "ESP32_Outdoor_Unit_Renamed",
  "mqtt_username": "dev_ch1_1",
  "mqtt_password": "<password>",
  "scope": "pubsub",
  "is_active": true,
  "created_at": "2026-11-12T04:38:34Z"
}

docs.title: Reset Device Password
docs.text:
POST /channels/{channel_id}/devices/{device_id}/reset-password
Authorization: Bearer <jwt_access_token>
Regenerates and updates the MQTT password for the specified device, returning the updated credentials. Previous credentials are immediately invalidated.

Response (200 OK): 

{
  "id": 1,
  "channel_id": 1,
  "name": "ESP32_Outdoor_Unit",
  "mqtt_username": "dev_ch1_1",
  "mqtt_password": "<newly_generated_password>",
  "scope": "pubsub",
  "is_active": true,
  "created_at": "2026-11-12T04:38:34Z"
}

docs.title: Fetch Channel History / Feeds
docs.text:
GET /channels/{channel_id}/history?limit=20&order=desc
X-API-Key: tl_read_xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx
Fetches historical telemetry data packets with full control over the number of records returned. Can also authenticate via Authorization: Bearer <jwt_access_token> or open access for public channels.

Query Parameters: - limit (optional integer, default 20, min 1, max 1000): Maximum number of recent data packets to return. - order (optional string, desc [newest first] or asc [oldest first], default desc). - start (optional ISO 8601 timestamp): Filter packets starting from this timestamp. - end (optional ISO 8601 timestamp): Filter packets up to this timestamp.

Response (200 OK): 

{
  "channel_id": 1,
  "count": 2,
  "limit": 20,
  "order": "desc",
  "feeds": [
    {
      "time": "2026-11-12T17:15:00.120Z",
      "payload": {
        "temperature": 25.4,
        "humidity": 61.2
      }
    },
    {
      "time": "2026-11-12T17:14:00.100Z",
      "payload": {
        "temperature": 25.1,
        "humidity": 61.5
      }
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: Fetch Latest Snapshot
docs.text:
GET /channels/{channel_id}/latest
X-API-Key: tl_read_xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx
Retrieves the single latest complete JSON packet recorded on the channel.

Response (200 OK): 

{
  "channel_id": 1,
  "timestamp": "2026-11-12T17:15:00.120Z",
  "fields": {
    "temperature": 25.4,
    "humidity": 61.2
  }
}

docs.title: Query Telemetry Series
docs.text:
GET /channels/{channel_id}/data?resolution=auto&fields=temperature,humidity&start=2026-11-11T00:00:00Z
Query Parameters: - resolution: auto, raw, 1m, or 1h. - fields: Comma-separated list of field names (optional). - start: ISO-8601 start timestamp. - end: ISO-8601 end timestamp.

docs.title: HTTP Telemetry Ingestion
docs.text:
POST /channels/{channel_id}/data
X-API-Key: tl_write_xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx
Content-Type: application/json
Request Body: Arbitrary JSON key-value pairs: 
{
  "temperature": 23.8,
  "humidity": 61.2,
  "battery_v": 3.78
}

docs.title: Export Telemetry Data (CSV / JSON)
docs.text:
GET /channels/{channel_id}/export?format=csv&resolution=raw
X-API-Key: tl_read_xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx
Query Parameters: - format: csv or json. - resolution: auto, raw, 1m, or 1h. - fields: Comma-separated list of field keys (optional). - start: ISO 8601 timestamp. - end: ISO 8601 timestamp.

Response (200 OK): Streaming CSV file attachment or JSON payload.

docs.title: Clear Channel Telemetry Data
docs.text:
DELETE /channels/{channel_id}/data
Authorization: Bearer <jwt_access_token>
Response (200 OK): 
{
  "status": "cleared",
  "channel_id": 1,
  "detail": "All telemetry points and messages have been cleared."
}

docs.title: Dispatch Downlink Device Commands
docs.text:
POST /channels/{channel_id}/commands
Authorization: Bearer <jwt_access_token>
Can also authenticate via X-API-Key: tl_write_....

Request Body: 

{
  "payload": {
    "relay": 1,
    "state": "ON"
  },
  "subtopic": "commands"
}
Publishes the payload directly to MQTT topic channels/{channel_id}/{subtopic} with QoS 1. Subscribed hardware nodes and clients receive the command immediately.

Response (200 OK): 

{
  "status": "dispatched",
  "channel_id": 1,
  "topic": "channels/1/commands",
  "payload": {
    "relay": 1,
    "state": "ON"
  }
}

docs.title: Import Historical Telemetry (CSV)
docs.text:
POST /channels/{channel_id}/import
Authorization: Bearer <jwt_access_token>
Content-Type: text/csv
Can also authenticate via X-API-Key: tl_write_.... Accepts generic CSV (time,temperature,humidity,...) or ThingSpeak CSV export format (created_at,entry_id,field1,field2,...). Auto-registers new channel fields.

Request Body (Raw text or JSON {"csv": "..."}): 

created_at,entry_id,field1,field2
2026-11-12T00:00:00Z,1,24.5,60.2
2026-11-12T01:00:00Z,2,25.1,58.9

Response (200 OK): 

{
  "status": "imported",
  "channel_id": 1,
  "points_imported": 2,
  "fields_discovered": ["field1", "field2"]
}

docs.title: MQTT Topics & Authorization Matrix
docs.text: This document outlines the MQTT topic structure and topic-level access control rules enforced by mosquitto-go-auth and mqtt.acl_topics().

docs.title: Topic Naming Conventions
docs.text:
All MQTT topics follow strict hierarchical namespaces:

channels/
└── {channel_id}/
    ├── data       # High-frequency JSON sensor telemetry
    ├── commands   # Downlink actuator commands (relays, triggers, configs)
    └── status     # Last Will and Testament (LWT) & online status

docs.title: Authorization Permission Matrix
docs.text:
mosquitto-go-auth passes an integer access flag into PostgreSQL: - 1 = Read - 2 = Write - 4 = Subscribe

Topic Pattern Client Identity Allowed Operations Condition / Evaluation Logic channels/{id}/data Hardware Device (d_*) Write (2) Device is active (is_active = true) and scope is publish or pubsub. channels/{id}/data Hardware Device (d_*) Sub (4), Read (1) Device is active and scope is subscribe or pubsub. channels/{id}/commands Hardware Device (d_*) Sub (4), Read (1) Device is active and scope is subscribe or pubsub. Receives downlink control payloads. channels/{id}/status Hardware Device (d_*) Write (2) Device is active and scope is publish or pubsub. Used for LWT messages. channels/{id}/data User Frontend Session (s_*) Sub (4), Read (1) Channel {id} is owned by user or has is_public = true. channels/{id}/status User Frontend Session (s_*) Sub (4), Read (1) Same as data channel. channels/{id}/commands API Service Account (svc_api) Write (2) Dispatches HTTP command requests to MQTT. $share/ingest/channels/+/data Ingestion Bridge (svc_bridge) Sub (4) Dedicated ingestion bridge shared consumer group. # (All Topics) Service Accounts (svc_bridge, svc_api) Superuser System services bypass topic checks.

docs.title: Example Ingestion Payloads
docs.text:
Payloads published to channels/{id}/data must be valid JSON objects. Numeric values are automatically cataloged as discrete time-series points:

{
  "temp_c": 22.45,
  "humidity_rh": 58.1,
  "lux": 340.0,
  "vibration": 0.003,
  "metadata": {
    "node_fw": "v1.4.2",
    "boot_count": 12
  }
}
  • temp_c, humidity_rh, lux, and vibration are parsed into individual time-series entries in telemetry.points.
  • The entire JSON payload (including metadata) is preserved verbatim in telemetry.messages.
